sources.note: Shows that benchmark contamination in reasoning models is alarmingly easy to hide: a brief round of GRPO erases the signals contamination detectors rely on, and PPO-style importance sampling and clipping are identified as the cause — implying a broad class of RL methods conceals contamination inherently.
sources.title: On The Fragility of Benchmark Contamination Detection in Reasoning Models

sources.note: Establishes that RL trades policy entropy for reward along a predictable exponential curve R = -a·exp(H) + b, derives that entropy change is driven by the covariance between action probability and advantage, and controls it by restricting updates to the highest-covariance tokens.
sources.title: The Entropy Mechanism of Reinforcement Learning for Reasoning Language Models

sources.note: Shows that the roughly 20% of CoT tokens with the highest entropy act as decision forks, and that restricting RLVR policy-gradient updates to only those tokens matches or beats full-gradient training, with the advantage growing with model size.
sources.title: Beyond the 80/20 Rule: High-Entropy Minority Tokens Drive Effective Reinforcement Learning for LLM Reasoning

sources.note: Reduces the question of whether an update raises or lowers entropy to the sign of one scalar per token, shows that under GRPO what matters is that scalar's deviation from a policy-weighted baseline rather than its own value, and proves the deviation averages to zero over a batch.
sources.title: On the Entropy Dynamics in Reinforcement Fine-Tuning of Large Language Models

sources.note: Shows by two four-armed bandits with nearly identical approximation error, one of which converges and one of which does not, that approximation error cannot characterize whether softmax policy gradient reaches the optimum, and replaces it with a condition on whether the features preserve the ordering of the rewards.
sources.title: Rethinking the Global Convergence of Softmax Policy Gradient with Linear Function Approximation

sources.note: Recasts entropy collapse as an imbalance of 'entropy flow' — tokens whose update lowers entropy persistently outweigh those that raise it — and rebalances the two sets with a closed-form coefficient computed from each batch, without reference policies or entropy bonuses.
sources.title: Understanding and Preventing Entropy Collapse in RLVR with On-Policy Entropy Flow Optimization

sources.note: Measures RLVR-trained models against their base models with pass@k at large k and finds the base wins, concluding RLVR sharpens sampling toward paths the base already had rather than adding new ones.
sources.title: Does Reinforcement Learning Really Incentivize Reasoning Capacity in LLMs Beyond the Base Model?

result.definition: The clipped-surrogate policy-gradient algorithm the RLVR methods here descend from. It is rarely run directly in these sources; what carries over is its clipping mechanism, which turns out to be an entropy control surface. Raising the upper clip alleviates collapse while lowering it produces the most severe collapse observed; clipping zeroes the gradient and so modulates the relative contribution of positive- against negative-advantage tokens; and clipped tokens are reported to have low probability, which is why relaxing the upper bound preserves specifically the updates that raise entropy. The same mechanism carries a cost recorded elsewhere in the archive: PPO-style importance sampling and clipping are identified as the reason a brief RL run erases the statistical signals contamination detectors rely on. One theoretical entry addresses the family rather than the algorithm, analysing the softmax policy gradient PPO is built on and finding its convergence decided by the feature representation rather than by how well that representation approximates anything.
